subject: Delta mapping & econ next actions — TechHelm evaluation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Amit Shah <amit@techhelm.com>, Lydia Gomez <lydia@cloudrise.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.inference
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TechHelm discovery — quick recap & proposed tests

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary (what we heard)
- Workload: customer-facing assistant for TechHelm cloud portal; mix of short (10-60 token) and medium (200-600 token) responses. Estimated monthly traffic ~2M tokens to start, with potential growth to 8-10M over 12 months.
- SLOs: p95 inference latency target ~<300ms for simple flows; conversational p95 budget ~600ms.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + customer audit expected, data residency in us-east.
- Key buyer concerns: unit cost (per-1M tokens), latency under burst, vendor lock / private deployment options, and deterministic regression risk on quantized models.

High-level competitive notes from our side (post-call)
- Hyperscaler A (CloudGiant): straightforward managed endpoints, but their per-token billing + variable batching can produce higher unit costs unless you buy a significant reserved commitment. Latency can be good for single requests but throughput economics often suffer.
- Hyperscaler B (OceanML): competitive on on-demand price but limited prefix caching and KV cache management we offer; caching is where we typically recover 20-40% of tokens for assistant-style workloads.
- Self-hosted open model (quantized): best raw unit cost if you manage infra well but ops burden and regression risk (quality/perf) are non-trivial for teams without inference expertise.

Redwood differentiators that map to your asks
- Smart routing + model variants so we can route low-latency flows to smaller models while keeping high-quality flows on the larger model (helps both latency and cost).
- Automatic KV/prefix caching: empirical wins in assistant workloads — we typically observe 25-45% effective token reduction when templates/prompts are repeated.
- Dedicated pools: reserved capacity with predictable per-token economics and burst isolation for tight SLOs.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns so teams see the unit economics per route/model.

Back-of-envelope econ (ballpark, to align expectations) — assumptions: 1M tokens = mix of prompt/response; batch-size effects + modest 30% cache hit.
- Redwood hosted (no commit): ~$95 per 1M tokens
- Redwood dedicated (3–12 month reserved commit, typical customer mix): ~$40–55 per 1M tokens effective
- Hyperscaler on-demand baseline: ~$120 per 1M tokens (varies by batch and reserved options)
- Self-hosted quantized (customer manages infra): ~$25–35 per 1M tokens + ops 

Proposed next tests (what we recommend to validate economics and perf)
1) 1M-token probe using a representative TechHelm prompt set (you supply ~10k representative requests or we sample) — measure raw token/second, p50/p95 latency, and effective cache-hit under live traffic. (Target: complete in 7–10 business days)
2) Batch-size sweep: run requests at batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16] to show cost/latency trade-offs for your workload.
3) Cache tuning: run a short workload with prefixes to measure hit-rate uplift (target: 20–40%) and corresponding cost delta.
4) Dedicated-run comparison: 72-hour dedicated pool run to show sustained throughput and committed-rate pricing.

Immediate asks for you
- Can you share a 10k request sample (anonymized) or a short synthetic generator by EOD Monday?
- Confirm whether SOC2 report/shared controls are required before pilot (we can produce SOC2 Type II evidence).
- Confirm the initial peak QPS you expect so we size the pilot correctly.

Attachments: I attached a short test plan and a lightweight econ worksheet that we can populate together.

If this matches, I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff + test-plan walkthrough next week and loop in Ben (pricing) and Laura (enterprise ops).

—
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference
From: Amit Shah <amit@techhelm.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: Lydia Gomez <lydia@cloudrise.ai>, Procurement <procurement@techhelm.com>
Date: Sat, 26 May 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TechHelm discovery — quick recap & proposed tests

Thanks Jonas — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Sample data: we can provide a 10k anonymized sample and a synthetic generator that produces our short/medium responses. Expect that by Monday.
- Peak QPS: typical peak 10–15 qps with short bursts to 30 qps during batch runs.
- SLOs: we want p95 < 300ms for the simple flows, conversational flows can accept up to 600ms.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II is required before production; for pilot we can accept SOC2 Type I + a readiness checklist.
- Procurement: we’d like to see two pricing options: (1) short trial (30 days) with usage cap and (2) committed pricing for 12 months. Please include any standard enterprise discounts.

Cc'd procurement to start the contracting thread.

—
Amit Shah
Head of AI, TechHelm
amit@techhelm.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Amit Shah <amit@techhelm.com>, Procurement <procurement@techhelm.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TechHelm discovery — quick recap & proposed tests

Appreciate the quick answers — looping Ben and Laura to handle pricing and procurement. Attaching the test-plan and a populated econ worksheet for TechHelm (see attachment names). High-level notes on pricing we can propose for procurement:

Pricing options (draft for procurement)
- 30-day pilot (trial): Hosted on Redwood API, hard cap at 3M tokens, no commit. Price: $95 per 1M tokens for overage beyond credits. We can provide $3,000 in credits to cover a portion of the pilot. No long-term commitment required.
- Pilot-to-dedicated ramp: If TechHelm opts into a 3-month reserved pool at pilot completion, we can offer an effective rate of $55 per 1M tokens (committed capacity pricing), subject to commit volume (monthly commit). This assumes we reach a 30% cache hit and typical batching behavior.
- Enterprise reserved (12-month): For 12-month commitment at predictable monthly usage, effective rate can drop to ~$40 per 1M tokens depending on total commit. This includes SLAs and a private network option.
- Self-hosted option: We provide a deployment package estimate; unit cost could be ~$25–35 per 1M tokens but with an ops uplift and support add-on.

Proposed test plan steps (we'll run together)
- Day 0: Kickoff + confirm dataset and traffic pattern.
- Day 1–3: 1M-token probe using provided sample (measure raw throughput, p50/p95, tokenized counts).
- Day 4–6: Batch sweep + cache tuning runs.
- Day 7: Dedicated 72-hour run (if you approve).

Action items
- Amit / TechHelm: share sample dataset and any redlines for SOC2 documentation.
- Procurement: please confirm the contact who owns PO/SOW and any mandatory terms.
- Ben / Laura: I’ve asked them to draft a short SOW and a pilot order form; Ben will propose the credit and discount structure.

Attachments: techhelm-test-plan.md, techhelm-econ-probe.xlsx, redwood-mini-sla.pdf

—
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: TechHelm negotiation play — priorities and levers

Internal note (do not forward) — short strategy for negotiation and what I want you to own: 
- Primary objective: get a short pilot that surfaces true effective token economics and p95 latency under their traffic. Winning pilot removes procurement objections.
- Pricing levers to offer: credits on pilot ($3k), short-term guaranteed reserved window (3 months) to bridge committed discount, commit tiers (monthly volume buckets) for 12-month price.
- Technical levers: commit to run a dedicated 72-hour sustained run (no rollout risk) to show throughput, and show caching uplift numbers with their sample prompts.
- Risk points: quantization regresses output in some paraphrase tests — avoid pushing aggressive quantization in pilot; use 8-bit optimized runner only if validated.
- Ask Ben: draft two canonical offer templates (pilot order form; 12-month commit schedule) and a short ‘how caching affects unit econ’ slide.
- Ask Laura: prep SOC2 artifacts and a short checklist for pilot security gating so procurement can sign off quickly.

Timeline: aim to have pilot SOW and pricing template ready by Fri, 31 May so procurement can review and sign in early June.

—
Jonas
From: Procurement <procurement@techhelm.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Amit Shah <amit@techhelm.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 1 Jun 2028 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TechHelm discovery — quick recap & proposed tests

Thanks — procurement here. We’re fine moving to a 30-day capped pilot if Redwood provides:
- A simple SOW with objectives and acceptance criteria.
- An explicit price cap for the pilot (we expect the $95/1M overage rate to be the max).
- SOC2 artifacts (type I for pilot; type II before prod).
- A one-page pilot order form showing credits and how overage is charged.

We’d like the 72-hour dedicated run scoped as an optional add-on (approved at pilot completion). Please send the SOW and pilot order form to procurement@techhelm.com and cc Amit. For the 12-month commit pricing, we’ll need a clear commit vs overage table and a cancellation clause.

Procurement will review the SOW and come back with any redlines within 3 business days.

—
TechHelm Procurement
